name: Fatty Acid Oxidation and Ketogenesis Disorder with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
aliases: FAO and Ketogenesis Defect with HCM
Inherited Fatty Acid Metabolism Disorder with Cardiac Hypertrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Fatty Acid Oxidation Disorders with Cardiac Involvement

criteria.description: Presence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Biochemical evidence of impaired fatty acid oxidation and ketogenesis (e.g., elevated acylcarnitines, hypoketotic hypoglycemia)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in fatty acid oxidation or ketogenesis pathways
Episodes of metabolic decompensation triggered by fasting or illness

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy plus biochemical evidence of fatty acid oxidation/ketogenesis impairment and/or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data.

pathognomonic.notes: Concentric left ventricular hypertrophy without dilation
Low ketone bodies despite hypoglycemia during metabolic stress

common.notes: Reduced endurance due to impaired energy metabolism
Including ventricular tachycardia and conduction abnormalities

occasional.notes: Enlarged liver due to fat accumulation

rare.notes: Sensory and motor deficits in distal limbs
Mild cognitive impairment in some patients

laboratory: Elevated plasma acylcarnitine profile indicating fatty acid oxidation defects
Hypoketotic hypoglycemia during fasting or illness
Elevated creatine kinase during muscle involvement
imaging: Echocardiography showing concentric left ventricular hypertrophy
Cardiac MRI confirming hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and fibrosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as ACADVL, HADHA, HADHB, or HMGCS2
other: Muscle biopsy may show lipid accumulation
Electrocardiogram abnormalities including arrhythmias and conduction delays

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations primarily in sarcomeric proteins
Presence of lactic acidosis rather than hypoketotic hypoglycemia

redFlags: Severe hypoketotic hypoglycemia during fasting or illness
Rapid progression of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with arrhythmias
Recurrent metabolic crises with lethargy and vomiting
references: Roe CR, et al. Fatty acid oxidation disorders: clinical and molecular aspects. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2020.
Spiekerkoetter U, et al. Clinical and molecular features of fatty acid oxidation disorders with cardiomyopathy. Mol Genet Metab. 2019.
Orphanet: Fatty acid oxidation and ketogenesis disorder with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (ORPHA:217591)
